_comment: Safety rules for the SafePlate hackathon demo (fictional data, not medical advice). A rule is used by the app only if reviewed is true. Reviewer: a pharmacy assistant with 20 years of community pharmacy experience. Sources were named from general knowledge and must be checked by the reviewer. 'keywords' and 'applies_when' are the machine-readable form of the approved 'food' and 'medicine_group' text.

rules.medicine_group: Statins: simvastatin, lovastatin (strong effect); atorvastatin (smaller effect)
rules.message: Grapefruit can raise statin levels in the blood and increase the risk of muscle side effects.
rules.swap: Orange (sweet), apple, pear or berries
rules.source: FDA consumer page 'Grapefruit Juice and Some Drugs Don't Mix'; statin product information

rules.medicine_group: Calcium-channel blockers: felodipine, nifedipine (dihydropyridines)
rules.message: Grapefruit can raise levels of these blood-pressure medicines and cause low blood pressure, dizziness or swelling.
rules.swap: Orange (sweet), apple, pear or berries
rules.source: FDA consumer page on grapefruit; BNF / product information for felodipine and nifedipine

rules.medicine_group: Other medicines known to interact with grapefruit (for example some immune, heart-rhythm and anxiety medicines), when the person's list says 'grapefruit-sensitive'
rules.message: This medicine may interact with grapefruit. Ask your pharmacist or doctor before including it.
rules.swap: Orange (sweet) or apple
rules.source: FDA consumer page on grapefruit; product information for the specific medicine

food: large portions of spinach, kale, broccoli, Brussels sprouts, cabbage, collard or turnip greens, parsley
rules.medicine_group: Warfarin
rules.message: Warfarin does not mean avoiding green vegetables. The aim is to keep vitamin K intake steady from week to week. Large changes can affect the INR. Keep the clinic informed of diet changes.
rules.swap: Keep portions regular rather than removing them
rules.source: NHS warfarin guidance; NIH Office of Dietary Supplements vitamin K fact sheet

rules.medicine_group: Warfarin
rules.message: Some reports link large amounts of cranberry to INR changes. The evidence is mixed, so treat this as a caution only.
rules.swap: Apple or pear juice, small servings
rules.source: Warfarin product information and interaction references; evidence is mixed

food: dishes served with wine, beer or spirits
rules.medicine_group: Sedatives: benzodiazepines, Z-drugs (zopiclone), sedating antihistamines, opioid painkillers, sedating antidepressants and antipsychotics, gabapentinoids
rules.message: Alcohol adds to drowsiness and can raise the risk of falls and breathing problems in older adults.
rules.swap: Alcohol-free version of the drink or dish
rules.source: Product information for these medicine groups; NHS alcohol and medicines guidance

food: large amounts of alcohol in dishes
rules.medicine_group: Metformin
rules.message: Heavy alcohol use with metformin raises the risk of lactic acidosis. Alcohol can also cause low blood sugar in people with diabetes.
rules.swap: Alcohol-free version
rules.source: Metformin product information

food: dishes cooked with wine, beer or spirits where most of the alcohol is cooked off
rules.medicine_group: Sedatives (as R06) and metformin (as R07)
rules.message: Cooking removes only part of the alcohol. Low risk for most people, but mention it for people on sedatives.
rules.swap: Stock-based version
rules.source: USDA alcohol retention in cooked food tables

food: salty or cured dishes: ham, bacon, salami, smoked fish, canned soup, stock cubes, soy sauce, pickles, olives, many takeaway dishes
rules.medicine_group: High blood pressure or heart failure (any blood-pressure or water tablets)
rules.message: High salt intake can raise blood pressure and cause fluid build-up.
rules.swap: Same dish seasoned with herbs, lemon, garlic or pepper; low-salt version
rules.source: NHS salt guidance (adults: no more than 6 g salt a day); WHO sodium guideline

rules.medicine_group: ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers (sartans), spironolactone and similar; kidney disease
rules.message: Potassium salt substitutes can push potassium too high with these medicines.
rules.swap: Herbs, spices, lemon, vinegar
rules.source: BNF warnings on potassium with these medicine groups; NHS information on LoSalt

food: large servings of potassium-rich foods: bananas, dried fruit, potatoes, tomato sauce, spinach, avocado, coconut water
rules.medicine_group: ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers (sartans), spironolactone and similar; kidney disease
rules.message: Ordinary servings are usually fine. Very large or frequent servings may raise potassium in some people.
rules.swap: Apple, berries, rice, pasta
rules.source: BNF; kidney charity dietary potassium guidance

food: aged cheese (mature cheddar, blue cheese, parmesan)
soy sauce, miso, tempeh, fermented tofu
rules.medicine_group: MAOI antidepressants (phenelzine, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid); also moclobemide at lower risk
rules.message: High tyramine foods can cause a sharp rise in blood pressure with MAOIs.
rules.swap: Fresh cheese such as cottage cheese, fresh meat or fish cooked the same day
rules.source: BNF; MAOI product information
rules.review_note: Reviewer: keep, but changed from EXCLUDE to WARN.

rules.medicine_group: Blood-pressure medicines, water tablets (diuretics), digoxin
rules.message: Real liquorice can raise blood pressure and lower potassium, which matters with water tablets and digoxin.
rules.swap: Fruit sweets or mint
rules.source: NHS liquorice advice; BNF

food: sugary drinks, sweet desserts, large portions of white rice, white bread or sugary sauces
rules.medicine_group: Diabetes, especially insulin or sulfonylureas
rules.message: Sugary or very starchy meals can push blood sugar up. Skipped or irregular meals can cause lows for people on insulin or sulfonylureas.
rules.swap: Fruit, unsweetened yoghurt, wholegrain options, smaller portions
rules.source: Diabetes UK healthy eating guidance; NICE type 2 diabetes guidance

rules.medicine_group: Needs: easy-to-chew foods (missing teeth, dentures, weak chewing)
rules.message: Hard or crunchy foods are difficult to chew and can be a choking risk.
rules.swap: Soft cooked vegetables, soft bread, soft biscuits dunked in tea, smooth nut butter thinned out
rules.source: NHS and British Dietetic Association texture guidance; IDDSI framework (levels 5 and 6)

rules.medicine_group: Needs: easy-to-chew foods
rules.message: Tough meat is hard to chew.
rules.swap: Slow-cooked stew, minced meat, flaked fish, meat in gravy
rules.source: IDDSI framework; BDA texture-modified diet guidance

rules.medicine_group: Needs: easy-to-chew foods or swallowing difficulty
rules.message: Small hard pieces can cause choking.
rules.swap: Boneless fish, peeled or chopped fruit, shredded chicken
rules.source: IDDSI framework; Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists guidance

food: very sticky foods: peanut butter on its own, soft white bread that forms a ball, sticky rice cakes, marshmallow, caramel, toffee
dry crumbly foods: dry cake, dry rice
rules.medicine_group: Needs: swallowing difficulty (dysphagia) or dry mouth
rules.message: Sticky or dry foods can stick in the mouth or throat.
rules.swap: Moist foods with sauce, smooth purees, soft moist cake with custard
rules.source: IDDSI framework; RCSLT guidance

food: any food that mixes thin liquid and solid pieces
rules.medicine_group: Needs: swallowing difficulty (dysphagia)
rules.message: Mixed thin liquid and solids are hard to control when swallowing. Whether thin drinks are allowed is for the person's speech and language therapist to say.
rules.swap: Smooth blended soup, porridge, thick and uniform textures
rules.source: IDDSI framework (level 4 and level 5); RCSLT guidance

rules.medicine_group: Tetracycline antibiotics (e.g. doxycycline) and ciprofloxacin (and other quinolones)
rules.message: Milk, yoghurt, cheese and calcium supplements can stop these antibiotics being absorbed properly. Take the antibiotic and these foods at least 2 hours apart.
rules.swap: Plan the meal 2 hours away from the antibiotic dose, or choose a dairy-free dish
rules.source: Product information / BNF for tetracyclines and ciprofloxacin. Leaflets for some products give longer gaps, so check.

rules.medicine_group: Levothyroxine
rules.message: Levothyroxine should be taken on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast and before coffee.
rules.swap: Plan breakfast and coffee 30 to 60 minutes after the tablet
rules.source: Levothyroxine product information; NHS levothyroxine guidance

food: dishes served with wine, beer or spirits
dishes cooked with wine, beer or spirits (e.g. risotto with white wine)
desserts containing liqueur or marsala (e.g. tiramisu)
rules.medicine_group: Warfarin
rules.message: Alcohol can change how warfarin works and affect the INR. Small amounts used in cooking are usually less of a concern, but drinks and desserts with liqueur should be discussed. Ask your pharmacist or doctor.
rules.swap: Alcohol-free version of the drink or dish
rules.source: Warfarin product information; NHS alcohol and warfarin guidance. Sources not yet checked.
rules.review_note: Added at the reviewer's request as a WARN. Kept separate from rule 6, which excludes alcohol for sedatives.
